$comment: Every page of the docs, in sidebar order, and the repository file each is ported from. scripts/sync-docs.mjs builds src/content/docs/docs/ from this file; nothing under it is written by hand. A source's sections narrow it to headings ('include'), drop headings ('omit'), or cut it between two lines ('from' up to 'to'). 'append' adds a file verbatim as a code block. 'exclude' lists every repository markdown file that is deliberately not a page, with the reason; the sync fails on a markdown file in neither list.

pages.title: OrkStack documentation
pages.description: Where to start, and how the documentation is organised: from a first Orkflow to operating a deployment.

pages.title: Install and run locally
pages.description: Start the whole local stack with one command, push the first-party activity images, and run a first Orkflow from the CLI and the UI.

pages.title: Examples
pages.description: Every example Orkflow in the repository, what it shows, what it needs to run, and its complete YAML.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.description: The components of OrkStack, what each one owns, and how a run flows through them from apply to retirement.

pages.title: Product boundary and invariants
pages.description: What OrkStack is and is not: the three primitives it builds on, its explicit non-goals, and the invariants no change may break.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.description: The words OrkStack uses on every surface, from Orkflow and Orker to pin, fan-out and release, each with its exact meaning.

parts.to: An Orkflow name is unique within a namespace.

pages.title: Orkflow DSL reference
pages.description: Every key of an Orkflow document, its validation rules and its runtime behaviour: tasks, inputs, outputs, joins, pins, awaits, fan-out, composition and caching.

pages.title: Orkflow patterns
pages.description: The rules the shipped examples follow, and why: deciding in a task, branching and re-joining, sagas, repetition without loops, and more.

pages.title: JSON and the enum dialect
pages.description: Why runtime data is always JSON, how YAML written in an authored document becomes JSON, and the enum spelling every client shares.

pages.title: OCI activity contract

pages.description: The shell example's activity written in Go and built FROM scratch, with its Dockerfile and program in full.

pages.title: activity-http
pages.description: One HTTP request, reported as data: its configuration, outputs and failure behaviour.

pages.title: activity-shell
pages.description: Run a command, a script or an expression in a shell image: its ops, configuration and outputs.

pages.title: activity-file
pages.description: Small, Unix-like file operations: copy, checksum, compression and archives, concatenation.

pages.title: activity-json
pages.description: Query and reshape JSON with jq as a task: its ops, variables and outputs.

pages.title: activity-git
pages.description: Resolve and check out git repositories over HTTPS as a task: its ops, credentials and outputs.

pages.title: activity-template
pages.description: Render text templates from a task's data: its ops, inputs and outputs.

pages.title: Triggers
pages.description: Inbound plain-HTTP run starters with bearer tokens: creating one, invoking it, and how a trigger differs from a webhook.

pages.title: Schedules
pages.description: Starting runs on a schedule: specs, fires, backfill, manual fires and what happens when fires overlap.

pages.title: Automation documents
pages.description: A namespace's settings, schedules, triggers and webhooks declared in one YAML document, planned, applied and exported with orkctl.

pages.title: Webhooks
pages.description: Run-event webhooks: scoping by namespace, Orkflow and task, signed bodies and how to verify them, delivery records and redelivery.

pages.title: Deployment and operations
pages.description: Topology, replicas and pools, releases and rollback, replay safety, and the day-to-day operations of a deployment.

pages.title: Configuration
pages.description: The one configuration file both binaries read, every setting with its environment variable and default, and the generated defaults file.

pages.title: Observability
pages.description: OpenTelemetry logs, metrics and traces, off by default: recipes, named sinks, per-namespace policy, and the local Grafana profile.

pages.title: Storage layout
pages.description: What OrkStack persists in object storage, under which key, who writes it and what removes it.

pages.title: Stats
pages.description: Where a dashboard's numbers come from: counts, failure fingerprints, flakes, usage and cache hit rates, all derived on read.

pages.title: Run evidence
pages.description: The run evidence bundle format, exporting one, and verifying it offline.

pages.title: UI and CLI parity
pages.description: The operator experience contract the UI and orkctl share: the same operations, selectors and errors on both surfaces.

pages.title: Security model
pages.description: The Orker as the security boundary, what a container never receives, the image policy, secrets, callers and the credentials OrkStack mints.

pages.title: Production checklist
pages.description: What to set up and decide before running a deployment carefully, from storage and image policy to releases and observability. Not a readiness claim.

pages.title: Upgrading and versioning

pages.title: Limitations
pages.description: Every hard limit and deliberate omission in one place, with the setting that moves it and the reason it exists.

pages.title: Troubleshooting and FAQ
pages.description: Symptoms as you see them, what causes each, how to confirm it and what to do: submitting, running, failures and the local stack.

pages.title: orkctl reference
pages.description: Every orkctl command and flag, generated from the CLI's own command tree.

pages.title: API reference
pages.description: Every client-facing Connect service, method, message and enum, generated from the proto sources' own comments.

pages.title: Error reasons

pages.title: Changelog
pages.description: Every notable change, in Keep a Changelog form; until 1.0 a breaking change is marked BREAKING.

pages.title: Contributing
pages.description: The change checklist: the fast checks, what CI runs on a pull request, and when a change is done.

pages.description: What is tested before a change merges, the proof tiers, why the evidence can be believed, and the invariants every test defends.

pages.title: Engineering contract
pages.description: AGENTS.md in full: the product boundary, runtime contracts, invariants and the evidence a change needs to be done.
